set_aside.subject: revocation visibility for an in-flight authenticated request
set_aside.text: “Immediate” revocation is defined as “every request authenticated after the revocation commits observes it,” while A11 still requires that a revoked object “blocks the next authorization check immediately” and A4 requires every project operation to evaluate current session, principal and project access.
set_aside.question: If a request authenticates before revocation commits but performs its project authorization check afterward, must that check observe the revocation?
options: Reject the request because every authorization check reads the post-commit revocation state.
Allow the already-authenticated request to finish under its pre-revocation authentication state; only requests authenticated after the commit must reject.
set_aside.default_guess: Reject at the post-commit authorization check.

witness.initial: A staff account has an active session and an active assignment to project P.
events: The staff request authenticates its session.
An administrator revokes the assignment and commits.
The first request then performs its project authorization check and attempts to read P.
outcomes: The guard re-reads the assignment, observes revocation, and rejects the read.
The request is treated as already authenticated before the commit and the read succeeds; only later-authenticated requests reject.
witness.observer: The staff caller sees either project data or an authorization rejection.

set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
set_aside.subject: archived progress read that creates an empty manual budget
set_aside.text: “project_tracking.list_project_progress creates the empty manual budget version when the project has none,” but `budget_management` owns the manual budget, activation and `ensure_manual_budget`; `project_tracking` owns the progress list, and only `budget_management` is named as an A13 consumer for `budget.manual_version_create`.
set_aside.question: Which module owns this read-triggered budget creation, and are creation, its audit record and the progress read performed in one `project_tracking` transaction or as a separately committed `budget_management.ensure_manual_budget` operation followed by the read?
options: `project_tracking` owns one transaction and creates the budget plus audit through budget-owned mechanisms available on that transaction.
`project_tracking` first delegates a separately committed creation to `budget_management`, then opens its progress-read transaction.
`budget_management` owns the combined operation and obtains the progress data needed for the result.
set_aside.default_guess: Make `project_tracking` own one atomic transaction while delegating budget construction rules to `budget_management`.

witness.initial: Archived project P has no manual budget version and no progress rows; authorized staff may read it.
events: The empty manual budget is inserted.
A persistence failure occurs while the progress rows are being read or the result is completed.
outcomes: Creation and read share one transaction, so the failure rolls back the budget and its audit record.
The delegated budget creation committed first, so the read fails but the empty budget and its audit record remain.
witness.observer: On the next read, staff either finds that the manual budget already exists or causes it to be created again.
